summary: Describes a way for application servers to locate and use media servers in SIP networks. Media servers provide basic building blocks such as announcements, user interaction, and conferencing. The memo defines an interoperable interface so those building blocks can be combined into larger applications. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Think of a main server that wants a sound system to play a message or mix a conference call. This memo says how to ask the sound system politely, in a way any brand understands.

subtitle: How a SIP application server asks a media server to play an announcement, run a voice dialog or mix a conference, using only the user part of the SIP address.

tldr.problem: Applications built on SIP need basic media building blocks such as announcements, prompt-and-collect and conference mixing, and need a standard way to locate and invoke them on a media server.
tldr.mechanism: The user part of the SIP Request-URI names the service (annc, dialog or conf), URI parameters carry the details, and the client simply sends an INVITE to the media server. SIP itself is not changed.
tldr.outcome: A media server that follows the convention can be used by any application server, while devices that ignore the convention are unaffected.

today: RFC 4240 is an Informational RFC (December 2005) and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Idea: Services Named by the User Part
sections.content:
In SIP networks there is a need for basic network media services: playing announcements, prompting and collecting information from a user, and mixing media streams for a basic conference. The RFC argues that these services are few in number, have not changed in 25 years of enhanced telephony services, and are not expected to change.

A multifunction media server has no users, so the left-hand side of the SIP URI (the user part) is used as a service indicator. The RFC stresses that this does not modify SIP, the meaning of the Request-URI, or any device that does not implement the convention. It says nothing about enhanced conferencing such as floor control, gain control or muting, which it leaves to other work (MSCML).
sections.eli5: Instead of inventing a new way to talk to sound machines, the memo reuses the name part of a SIP address as a label for what you want.

sections.title: The Service Indicator
sections.content:
The service indicator is the service name plus an optional service instance identifier, separated by an equal sign. It is case insensitive, as SIP requires. The service name MUST use only alphanumeric characters plus dash and MUST NOT include an equal sign. The instance identifier MUST be a legal user part of a SIP URI, and is used when a service has separate instances, such as several conferences on one server. A service indicator MAY have parameters, which follow the SIP URI parameter convention of semicolon-separated keyword=value pairs.

When the media server gets an INVITE, it notes the service indicator and either honors the request or fails it:

  • If it cannot perform the service or does not recognize the indicator, it MUST respond with 488 NOT ACCEPTABLE HERE. The RFC explains that 606 is not appropriate, because another media server might be able to do it.
  • If a service needs an existing instance and none exists, it MUST respond with 404 NOT FOUND.

For security, the media server SHOULD use the protections in RFC 3261, MAY issue 401 challenges, SHOULD support the sips: scheme for the announcement service and MUST support it for the dialog and conference services.
sections.eli5: The label says what you want, and you can add a number to pick one particular room. If the machine does not offer that, it says no politely.

sections.title: The Announcement Service
sections.content:
The announcement service delivers a multimedia resource, such as a prompt file, to a terminal. It uses the user part annc and can play one object (which may have several streams, such as audio and video), but not several objects on the same SIP dialog. The usual flow has a caller INVITE a proxy, the proxy INVITE the media server, a 200 OK and ACK follow, the media server plays the prompt and then sends a BYE. The RFC notes the service also works if the caller invokes it directly.

Parameters control the announcement:

  • play is mandatory and names the resource or sequence. If it is missing, the server MUST respond with 400.
  • repeat sets how many times to repeat; forever is allowed, and the server is RECOMMENDED to limit it so errant clients cannot mount a denial of service attack.
  • delay and duration are in milliseconds.
  • locale selects language and optional country variant, such as en_CA, with best-match fallback.
  • param1 to param9 pass values to substitute into a sequence.
  • extension parameters that the server does not understand MUST be silently ignored.

The play value is a URL (http, https, ftp, file or nfs) or a provisioned sequence of the form /provisioned/ followed by an identifier. A missing announcement gets 404, and a retrieval error gets 400.
sections.eli5: You ask the sound room to play a particular recording, say how many times and in which language, and it hangs up when it is done.

sections.title: Prompt and Collect, and Conferences
sections.content:
Prompt and collect (also called a voice dialog) uses the user part dialog and a voicexml parameter holding the URI of the VoiceXML script to run. Extra parameters can be passed to the VoiceXML session as session variables, and a keyword with no value MUST be rejected with 400. Because scripts, grammars and results can carry sensitive data such as pass codes, the media server MUST support https for fetching scripts, grammars and later documents, and for posting results.

The conference service uses the form sip:conf=uniqueIdentifier@mediaserver.example.net. An INVITE to a URI that does not yet exist creates a mixing session if resources are available; an INVITE to an existing one joins it. A BYE removes a leg, and the session lasts while at least one dialog is associated with it. The identifier must be unique, and keeping it unique is the job of the conference control application. In conferencing-framework terms, the media server acts as a focus and MUST support the ;isfocus parameter, while the application server acts as the conference factory. A request with conf but no identifier MUST get 404. Because conferences can have billing implications, the media server SHOULD authenticate the application server, and at minimum MUST implement sips:.
sections.eli5: For a phone menu, you point the sound room at a script that says what to ask. For a conference, everyone calls the same numbered room and gets mixed together.

sections.title: Why a Fixed User Part
sections.content:
Section 7 defends the choice of fixed user names (the RFC names annc, ivr, dialog and conf). Critics argued the user part should be opaque and local, and that reserving names removes them from the user address space. The RFC answers that the names only have meaning at media servers that choose to implement the convention. The name "annc" at a user's own device or domain does not collide, because a media server's namespace is separate from an organization's, and a proxy can map any opaque public name to the media server's name.

It also argues that provisioned, arbitrary names work in a closed network but not across domains, where a client would have to know the local name for each service. Using the user part lets standard SIP machinery work unchanged: media servers can register their capabilities as users, and two servers registered for annc with a redirect server give failover when one fails. The URI to play is a parameter so ordinary proxies are not overburdened.
sections.eli5: Having the same door labels everywhere means anyone can find the right door, even in a building they have never visited.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Exposing services at well-known addresses may not be desirable, so the media server SHOULD authenticate and authorize requesting endpoints per local policy. Some interactions carry confidential data and need integrity protection, so the media server MUST implement sips: and developers are RECOMMENDED to use its security services.

The RFC warns that billing is often based on completed calls, which means a 2xx result, so the early media announcement service is an issue, and it says this is one reason why that service is deprecated. Repeating an announcement forever invites denial of service, so the server SHOULD have local policies such as time-limiting "forever", analyzing where requests come from, or white-lists.
sections.eli5: The sound room should check who is asking, keep private things private, and not play a recording forever just because someone asked.
